XX.|OF THE APOSTLES.|351}}</noinclude>{{dropinitial|A|image=Rhemes New Testament 1582 initial A, a bearded man.png|imgsize=115px|fl={{verse|chapter=20|verse=1}}}}ND after that the tumult was ceased, Paul calling the disciples, and exhorting them, tooke his leaue, and set forvvard to goe into Macedonia. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=2}}† And vvhen he had vvalked through those partes, & had exhorted them vvith much speach, he came to Greece:

{{verse|chapter=20|verse=3}}† vvhere when he had spent three moneths, the Iewes laid wait for him as he was about to saile into Syria: and he had councel to returne through Macedonia. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=4}}† And there accompanied him Sosipater of Pyrrhus, of Berœa: and of Thessalonians, Aristarchus, and Secundus: and Caius of Derbè, and Timothee: and of Asia, Tychicus and Tróphimus. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=5}}† These going before, staied for vs at Troas: {{verse|chapter=20|verse=6}}† but vve sailed after the daies of Azymes from Philippi, and came to them vnto Troas in fiue daies, vvhere vve abode seuen daies.

{{verse|chapter=20|verse=7}}† And in the first of the Sabboth vvhen we vvere assembled to {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ S. Paul did here breake bread on the Sunday as it is broken in the Sacramēt of the body of Christ, and had both before & after the celebrating of the Sacramēt a sermon to the people. ''Aug. ep. 86 ad Casulanū. Vener. Beda in 20 Act''.}}∷ breake bread, Paul disputed with them, being to depart on the morow, and he continued the sermon vntil midnight. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=8}}† And there vvere a great number of lampes in the vpper chamber vvhere vve vvere assembled. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=9}}† And a certaine yong man named Eútychus, sitting vpon the window, vvhereas he vvas oppressed vvith heauy sleepe ( Paul disputing long) driuen by sleepe, fel from the third loft downe, and was taken vp dead. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=10}}† To whom when Paul was gone dovvne, he lay vpon him: and embracing him he said, Be not troubled, for his soule is in him. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=11}}† And going vp and breaking bread and tasting, and hauing talked sufficiently to them vntil day light, so he departed. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=12}}† And they brought the lad aliue, and were not a litle comforted.

{{verse|chapter=20|verse=13}}† But we going vp into the ship, sailed to Asson, from thence meaning to receiue Paul. for so he had ordained, him self purposing to iourney by land. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=14}}† And vvhen he had found vs in Asson, taking him with vs vve came to Mityléne. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=15}}† And sailing thence, the day folovving vve came ouer against Chios: and the other day we arriued at Samos: and the day folovving vve came to Milétum. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=16}}† for Paul had purposed to saile leauing Ephesus, lest any stay should be made him in Asia. For he hastened, if it vvere possible for him, to keepe the day of {{sup|‖}} Pentecost at Hierusalem.

{{verse|chapter=20|verse=17}}† {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=The Epistle for S. Steven Pope. Aug. 2.}}And sending from Milétum to Ephesus, he called the {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ That is, ''Priests'' as ''Act. 15, 4''. See the marginal annot. there.}}∷ {{MarginNote|margin=right|margin-width=65|text=∷ ''πρεσβυτέρους''}}∷ Auncients of the Church. {{verse|chapter=20|verse=18}}† Who being come to him, and<noinclude>{{rh|||assembled}}</noinclude>
